title: I_max saturation is not work-bound saturation: information-maximal protocol extracts no work

comments.author: human
comments.body:
In Theorem 1 (`thm:Imax-discrete`), the 'Achievability of $I_A=N\log2$' construction sets $D_k=\mathbf 1\{X_{v_k}-X_{u_k}>0\}$ — the sign of a Brownian increment over a sub-window chosen **independently of the potential geometry and of the absolute position**. These bits are i.i.d. uniform, so $I_A=H(A)=N\log2$. **But this control is statistically independent of where the particle sits in $V$, so it does not rectify thermal motion: $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle\approx 0$**, nowhere near $k_BT\,N\log2$.

The solution conflates two distinct 'saturations': (A) attaining $I_A=I_{\max}=N\log2$ (information), and (B) saturating the work bound $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle=k_BT I_A$ (thermodynamics, requires reversibility, condition (iii)). The explicit construction proves (A) with a protocol incompatible with (B). Proposition 1 (`prop:opt`) then asserts a protocol satisfying (i)+(ii)+(iii) simultaneously exists, but the only construction offered for (i) is the random-increment rule, which cannot satisfy (iii). **No protocol is ever exhibited or shown to exist that simultaneously attains $I_A=N\log2$ AND extracts $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle=k_BT N\log2$.**

This is the heart of parts (b)/(c), which explicitly demand exhibiting saturating protocols. There is a likely genuine obstruction: rectifying work forces the control to depend on position relative to $V$, which generically correlates successive decisions (exactly the 'sign rule' the solution itself shows has $H(D)<N\log2$). So a trade-off probably holds and Prop 1's simultaneous-saturation claim is unproven and likely false as stated. The correct work/power/efficiency-saturating protocols are generally NOT the $I_A$-maximizers and must be constructed explicitly.
